subject: SIG follow-up: encryption (in-transit / at-rest), KMS/HSM, rotation evidence
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@novushealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: encryption specifics and evidence request

Mina —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team needs a few concrete artifacts and clarifications to complete the SIG v1.5 sections on encryption and key management. Can you confirm the following and provide the listed evidence by end of day Wednesday (Feb 8)? If you prefer, we can take a short call to walk through.

1) In transit: confirm TLS version(s) supported for API endpoints, cipher suites, and whether mutual TLS is supported for Dedicated/Private deployments. Evidence: TLS config dump (or guidance) and an example endpoint with curl showing negotiated cipher.

2) At rest: which data stores are encrypted by default (model weights, logs, blob storage). Evidence: high-level architecture diagram showing encrypted boundaries and a statement of encryption algorithms in use.

3) KMS/HSM: are keys stored in a managed KMS or backed by an HSM? If HSM-backed, please provide the attestation/third-party statement (FIPS 140-2/3 or equivalent) and a short description of the custody model (Redwood-managed vs BYOK).

4) Key rotation: frequency for customer-facing keys vs platform root/KEKs, process summary, and an extract of rotation logs (redacted is fine) showing a recent rotation cycle. Evidence: key_rotation_logs (redacted), rotation runbook pointer.

5) Access controls: who can perform key rotations or export operations, and an access matrix. Evidence: a brief ACL snapshot or the KMS IAM roles document.

We are happy to accept redacted logs and attestations if there are sensitive fields. For uploads, we can consume a secure Drive link or SFTP — whatever works for you.

If you can flag anything that will take longer, that helps us triage and request a scoped exception if needed.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Director, Security Engineering
Novus Health

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Feb 2028 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption specifics and evidence request

Samir —

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide everything you asked for; below is what we will deliver and an estimated ETA. I copied Kimberly from Security Ops who will pull the HSM attestation and rotation logs.

Deliverables (high level)
- redwood_enc_summary_for_SIG.pdf — architecture diagram + encryption algorithm list (ETA: Mon, Feb 6)
- key_rotation_logs_redacted.csv — rotation events for KEK and customer CMKs (redacted) (ETA: Tue, Feb 7)
- hsm_attestation_3yr.pdf — third-party HSM attestation and FIPS summary (ETA: Tue, Feb 7)
- kms_access_matrix.xlsx — role matrix for KMS operations (ETA: Tue, Feb 7)
- Curl example and TLS config notes included in PDF

Short answers inline:
- In-transit: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported on hosted API and Private; we prefer TLS 1.3. Cipher suites follow modern recommendations (AEAD-based ciphers). Mutual TLS is supported on Private deployments (customer-configured).
- At-rest: model artifacts, object stores, and audit logs are encrypted at rest by default (AES-256). Customer-provided models remain in customer tenants; Dedicated/Private supports BYOK.
- KMS/HSM: We use a managed KMS with HSM-backed root keys in our Private and Dedicated offerings. For hosted customers, keys are in our managed KMS; BYOK for Dedicated/Private is available via envelope encryption and customer-managed HSMs if required.
- Rotation: KEKs rotated on a quarterly cadence by default, CMKs on a 12-month schedule (customers can request different policies). Rotation runbook will be included.

If this timeline works, I will share a Drive folder with the artifacts and a single PDF summary for your SIG reviewer. If Novus needs native formats (CSV/Excel) we’ll include those as redacted extracts.

Thanks — I’ll follow up once Kimberly uploads the attestation.

— Mina Haddad
Sr. Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0137

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Feb 2028 08:32:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: SIG artifacts — pull plan and redaction

Kimberly / Marissa —

Per Samir's request we need the HSM attestation and rotation logs by EOD Tue (Feb 7) so we can deliver to Novus. Quick plan:

- Kimberly: can you export the HSM attestation package (latest cert + third-party statement) and confirm FIPS coverage? Add a one-paragraph cover note describing custody model (Redwood-managed HSM for hosted; HSM-backed KEKs in Dedicated/Private; BYOK options). Please place the PDF in /security/sig/novus/ and ping me when done.
- Marissa: please generate a redacted CSV of key rotation events for the past 12 months (columns: rotation_id, key_id (hashed), rotated_at, actor_role). Replace any principal identifiers with role labels. Also produce the ACL snapshot for the KMS (xlsx). Put both files in the same folder and set Drive sharing to 'view only' for the external link.

A couple of notes: do not export private key material or any raw key blobs. Redaction must remove any user-IDs and IP addresses. We will include a short signed statement from legal confirming redaction.

If either of you needs help running the export queries, I can coordinate with Platform infra (I'll open a ticket).

Thanks — tight turnaround but doable.

— Mina

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novushealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Feb 2028 15:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: encryption specifics and evidence request

Samir —

Attached is the package we discussed and the Drive link below. Contents:
- redwood_enc_summary_for_SIG.pdf (architecture diagram, TLS notes, at-rest encryption details, rotation policy summary)
- key_rotation_logs_redacted.csv (past 12 months, principal identifiers replaced with role labels)
- hsm_attestation_3yr.pdf (vendor attestation / FIPS summary)
- kms_access_matrix.xlsx (roles permitted to perform rotation/export operations)

Drive link (view-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleLinkSIGPackage
DocuSign (signed cover letter for redaction): https://app.docusign.com/some-envelope-id-EXAMPLE

Quick recap of key points:
- TLS: endpoints support TLS 1.2 and 1.3; we prefer and recommend 1.3 where available.
- HSM: root/KEKs are HSM-backed for Dedicated/Private; hosted keys are in a managed KMS with HSM-backed root at the provider level. Attestation attached.
- Rotation cadence: KEK quarterly, CMKs annually; customers can request custom schedules.
- Access: rotation and export require a multi-role approval in our KMS (see ACL spreadsheet).

If Novus wants a live walk-through of the documents or a short session to validate the rotation log format, I’m available Thu morning PST. Please confirm receipt and whether the redaction level is acceptable for the SIG reviewer.

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Sr. Security Program Manager
Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_enc_summary_for_SIG.pdf (application/pdf); key_rotation_logs_redacted.csv (text/csv); hsm_attestation_3yr.pdf (application/pdf); kms_access_matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
